# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("McCarthy_2016_artefenomel"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("McCarthy_2016_artefenomel"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkw174> (open access, PMC4992851)

Artefenomel (OZ439) is a synthetic ozonide antimalarial. McCarthy 2016
gave single oral doses of 100, 200 or 500 mg to healthy volunteers who
had been inoculated with *Plasmodium falciparum*-infected erythrocytes
(the induced blood-stage malaria, or IBSM, challenge model), and fitted
a population PK model followed by a parasite growth-and-kill PK/PD model.

# Population

Twenty-four healthy adults (eight per dose cohort) were enrolled and
completed the study at QIMR Berghofer, Brisbane (ACTRN12612000814875).
Supplementary Table S1: age 20-34 years (mean 25.5, SD 3.7), 12 male and
12 female, all Caucasian, body weight 53.9-97.6 kg (mean 73.1, SD 12),
BMI 19.1-28.2 kg/m^2. Volunteers were inoculated with about 1800 viable
parasitised erythrocytes and dosed once qPCR parasitaemia (18S rRNA
gene, all stages) reached 1000 parasites/mL. Artefenomel was given as a
suspension of the mesylate after 200 mL of full-cream milk.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("McCarthy_2016_artefenomel")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/McCarthy_2016_artefenomel.R`; this table
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (ka) | 0.18 1/h | Table 2 'Ka' (= Table S5) |
| `ltlag` (ALAG) | 0.40 h | Table 2 'ALAG' |
| `lcl` (CL/F0, 500 mg reference) | 40.9 L/h | Table 2 'CL/F' |
| `lvc` (Vc/F) | 189 L | Table 2 'Vc/F' |
| `lvp` (Vp/F) | 1573 L | Table 2 'Vp/F' |
| `lq` (Q/F) | 12.7 L/h | Table 2 'Q/F' |
| `e_dose_cl` | -0.55 | Table 2 'Dose on CL/F' = 0.55; footnote c prints the exponent as -0.55 |
| `lkgrow` (G) | 0.06 1/h, fixed | Table 3 'G' (= Table S6) |
| `lemax` (D) | 0.20 1/h | Table 3 'D' |
| `lec50` (EC50) | 6.19 ng/mL | Table 3 'EC50' |
| `lhill` (H) | 2.03 | Table 3 'H' |
| `etalvc`, `etalvp`, `etalcl`, `etaltlag` | 0.269, 0.071, 0.064, 0.001 | Table 2 IIV column (variances, footnote a) |
| `etalemax`, `etalec50` | 0.017, 0.408 | Table 3 IIV column; Table S6 |
| `propSd`, `propSd_parasites` | 0, fixed | not reported |
| CL/F = CL/F0 x (dose/500)^-0.55 | -- | Table 2 footnote c |
| Two-compartment PK, first-order absorption with lag | -- | Methods 'Pharmacometric analysis' |
| dP/dt = P (G - D C^H / (C^H + EC50^H)) | -- | Supplementary data, Equation 1 |
| MIC = EC50 (G / (D - G))^(1/H) | 4.08 ng/mL | Supplementary data, Equation 3 and text |
| MPC_X = EC50 (X / (1 - X))^(1/H) | 60, 26 ng/mL | Supplementary data, Equation 2; Results (MPC99%, MPC95%) |

# Closed-form checks of the PD parameters

The supplement derives the MIC (the concentration at which growth and
kill cancel, so dP/dt = 0) and the minimal parasiticidal concentrations
MPC_X (the concentration reaching a fraction X of the maximum kill rate)
from Equation 1, and the paper reports MIC = 4.08 ng/mL, MPC99% = 60
ng/mL and MPC95% = 26 ng/mL. Recomputing them from the packaged `ini()`
values confirms the PD parameters and the form of Equation 1.

```{r closed_form}
mod <- readModelDb("McCarthy_2016_artefenomel")
ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf
p <- setNames(ini_df$est, ini_df$name)

g <- exp(p[["lkgrow"]])
d <- exp(p[["lemax"]])
ec50 <- exp(p[["lec50"]])
h <- exp(p[["lhill"]])

mic <- ec50 * (g / (d - g))^(1 / h)
mpc <- function(x) ec50 * (x / (1 - x))^(1 / h)

pd_check <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("MIC", "MPC99%", "MPC95%"),
  Published = c(4.08, 60, 26),
  Recomputed = c(mic, mpc(0.99), mpc(0.95))
)
knitr::kable(pd_check, digits = 2, caption = "Supplementary data Equations 2-3 vs. the reported values.")

stopifnot(
  abs(mic - 4.08) < 0.01,
  abs(mpc(0.99) - 60) < 1,
  abs(mpc(0.95) - 26) < 0.5
)
```

# Typical-value checks

The typical subject (`zeroRe()`) is solved for each dose with a dense
grid. Two checks use the same parameters on both sides, so they hold to
numerical precision:

* mass balance: AUC(0-inf) x CL/F returns the dose, with CL/F the
  dose-adjusted value 40.9 x (dose/500)^-0.55;
* the parasitaemia nadir falls exactly where the falling concentration
  crosses the MIC, because Equation 1 has dP/dt = 0 only at C = MIC.

```{r typical}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
doses <- c(100, 200, 500)
para0 <- c(`100` = 2.6, `200` = 6.7, `500` = 4.3)

grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.02), seq(48, 6000, by = 0.5))))

make_typ_events <- function(dose) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = grid, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      DOSE_ARTEFENOMEL_MG = dose,
      PARA = para0[[as.character(dose)]]
    )
}

typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(doses, function(dose) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, make_typ_events(dose), returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose = dose)
}))

trap <- function(x, y) sum(diff(x) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

typ_chk <- typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc = trap(time, Cc),
    cl_model = 40.9 * (dose[1] / 500)^-0.55,
    cmax = max(Cc),
    tmax = time[which.max(Cc)],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    mass_balance = auc * cl_model / (dose * 1000),
    cl_apparent = dose * 1000 / auc
  )

knitr::kable(
  typ_chk |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Dose (mg)" = dose, "AUC0-inf (h*ng/mL)" = auc, "CL/F model (L/h)" = cl_model,
      "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC x CL / dose" = mass_balance,
      "Dose / AUC (L/h)" = cl_apparent
    ),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Typical-subject exposure by dose."
)

stopifnot(all(abs(typ_chk$mass_balance - 1) < 0.01))

# Nadir vs MIC crossing for the 200 mg typical subject.
typ200 <- typ |> dplyr::filter(dose == 200, time <= 300)
t_nadir <- typ200$time[which.min(typ200$parasites)]
after_peak <- typ200 |> dplyr::filter(time > typ200$time[which.max(typ200$Cc)])
t_mic <- after_peak$time[which(after_peak$Cc < mic)[1]]
c(nadir_h = t_nadir, mic_crossing_h = t_mic)
stopifnot(abs(t_nadir - t_mic) <= 0.5)
```

The dose-normalised apparent clearance falls with dose as the paper
describes (Results 'PK', Figure S1C). The typical CL/F values (99, 68
and 41 L/h) are 7-11% above the non-compartmental geometric means of
Table 1 (91, 61 and 38 L/h):

```{r typical_cl}
cl_nca <- c(91, 61, 38)
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_chk$cl_model / cl_nca - 1) < 0.2))
```

# Virtual cohort

Each dose arm has 200 virtual subjects. The model needs two covariates:
the dose itself (`DOSE_ARTEFENOMEL_MG`, which drives CL/F) and the
parasitaemia at dosing (`PARA`, in parasites/uL; the model multiplies by
1000 to work in parasites/mL). The paper does not tabulate the baseline
parasitaemia, so each arm is started at its cohort median at t = 0 read
by the maintainers from Figure 2 (about 2600, 6700 and 4300 parasites/mL
for 100, 200 and 500 mg). The observation times are the paper's PK
schedule (Methods 'Study plan'), with sampling to 456 h added for the
500 mg cohort as in Figure 1, plus a denser grid for the plots.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160825)
n_per_arm <- 200

pk_times <- c(0, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108, 120, 132, 144)
plot_times <- c(seq(0, 48, by = 1), seq(52, 456, by = 4))

make_arm <- function(dose, arm_index) {
  ids <- (arm_index - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(pk_times, plot_times, if (dose == 500) 456)))
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      DOSE_ARTEFENOMEL_MG = dose,
      PARA = para0[[as.character(dose)]],
      treatment = paste(dose, "mg")
    )
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) make_arm(doses[i], i))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events,
  keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"
))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1 -- artefenomel concentration by dose

Replicates Figure 1 of McCarthy 2016 (observed median concentrations by
dose cohort). The lines are the simulated median and 5th-95th
percentiles.

```{r fig1}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Artefenomel plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of McCarthy 2016."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Figure 2 -- parasitaemia by dose

Replicates Figure 2 of McCarthy 2016 (median parasitaemia by dose
cohort). The 100 mg cohort was rescued with artemether/lumefantrine at
60 h, and all subjects eventually received rescue treatment; the
simulation has no rescue, so it continues past the observed follow-up.
The dashed line is the qPCR detection limit (10 parasites/mL).

```{r fig2}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 300) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = median(parasites), lo = quantile(parasites, 0.05), hi = quantile(parasites, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1e-3, 1e6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after artefenomel administration (h)", y = "Parasitaemia (parasites/mL)",
    colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of McCarthy 2016."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

For the typical subject the model gives:

* 500 mg: parasitaemia falls below the 10 parasites/mL detection limit at
  46 h, against about 42 h for the observed median.
* 200 mg: parasitaemia reaches a nadir of about 160 parasites/mL at 36 h
  and then regrows. The observed median reached about 55 parasites/mL at
  48 h and recrudesced after 60 h.
* 100 mg: the model diverges from the data. The typical subject falls
  about 12-fold to a nadir at 24 h before regrowing. The observed median
  instead rose to about 10 000 parasites/mL, and the cohort was rescued
  at 60 h. The paper did no PD analysis of this cohort, so the PK/PD
  parameters were informed mainly by the 200 and 500 mg data.

With 500 mg the paper observed recrudescence between days 6 and 10 in
four of eight volunteers. The table below gives the fraction of simulated
subjects whose parasitaemia falls below the paper's cure threshold of
0.003 parasites/mL within 456 h. About six in ten of the simulated
500 mg subjects clear, close to the four of eight observed. This is for
orientation only: the paper reports no such figure for this setting, and
its Figure S4 cure probabilities came from a different, unpublished
patient PK model.

```{r cure}
sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cleared = any(parasites < 0.003), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(`Fraction below 0.003 parasites/mL` = mean(cleared), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the simulated concentrations at the
paper's sampling times (0-144 h for 100 and 200 mg; to 456 h for 500 mg,
matching the Table 1 footnote).

```{r pknca}
# Sampling schedule per arm; pk_times starts at 0, so every subject keeps
# its time-zero record.
schedule <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(treatment = paste(doses, "mg"), time = pk_times),
  data.frame(treatment = "500 mg", time = 456)
)

nca_conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::inner_join(schedule, by = c("treatment", "time")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))

nca_dose <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA (Table 1)

Table 1 reports geometric means; the simulated column is the virtual-
cohort median, which for log-normal exposure estimates the same central
value. The dose is in mg and the concentration in ng/mL, so PKNCA's
clearance (mg / (h*ng/mL)) is multiplied by 1000 to give L/h.

```{r nca_compare}
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs", PPORRES * 1000, PPORRES))
nca_res$result <- nca_tbl

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life, ~cl.obs,
  "100 mg", 164, 4, 1100, 52, 91,
  "200 mg", 448, 4, 3286, 51, 61,
  "500 mg", 1263, 4, 13239, 260, 38
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(
    cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "h*ng/mL",
    half.life = "h", cl.obs = "L/h"
  ),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (virtual-cohort median) vs. McCarthy 2016 Table 1",
    "(geometric means; Tmax is the reported average). * differs by >20%."
  )
)

sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(published |> dplyr::select(treatment, aucinf.obs), by = "treatment")

# Structural check on the centre of the distribution: a mis-transcribed
# clearance, volume or dose exponent moves the median AUC by far more.
stopifnot(all(abs(sim_auc$med / sim_auc$aucinf.obs - 1) < 0.3))
```

AUC(0-inf) and CL/F agree with Table 1 within 7-13% at every dose,
confirming the dose-dependent clearance.

Cmax is under-predicted by 42-47% at all three doses, although the
observed Tmax of 4 h is reproduced. With ka = 0.18 1/h, the published
model absorbs too slowly to reach the observed peaks. The only visual
predictive check in the paper (Figure S2) is on a log scale too coarse
to resolve the peak. The shortfall is therefore reported here and left
uncorrected.

The NCA half-lives do not match either. The model gives about 100-120 h
at every dose, while Table 1 gives 51-52 h for 100 and 200 mg and 260 h
for 500 mg. Two things contribute. The terminal estimate depends on the
sampling window, and the 100 and 200 mg cohorts were followed for only
144 h. The paper's own half-lives also vary widely between subjects
(coefficients of variation 63-84%).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error.** The paper reports no residual-error model for
  either the PK or the PK/PD fit. Both residual SDs are fixed to zero, so
  stochastic simulations carry between-subject variability only.
* **Initial parasitaemia.** The paper does not say how the parasitaemia
  at dosing entered the PK/PD fit (estimated, fixed to the observed
  value, or otherwise). The model takes it as the per-subject covariate
  `PARA` (parasites/uL, multiplied by 1000 inside the model). The cohort
  medians used in this vignette were read from Figure 2 and are
  approximate.
* **Form of the random effects.** The IIV columns of Tables 2 and 3 are
  variances of the random effects; they are implemented as exponential
  (log-normal) effects, the usual NONMEM convention, which the paper does
  not state explicitly. No covariances are reported, so all random
  effects are independent.
* **Dose effect only on clearance.** The Discussion mentions
  "dose-dependent rates of absorption and clearance", but Table 2 and
  its footnote give a dose effect on CL/F only, so only that effect is
  implemented. The Table 2 row prints the dose coefficient as 0.55 and
  the footnote prints the equation with exponent -0.55; the negative
  sign matches the falling CL/F with dose in Table 1 and Figure S1C.
* **Salt or base.** Artefenomel was given as the mesylate; the paper does
  not say whether the 100/200/500 mg doses are salt or free-base masses.
  The model is parameterised on the nominal doses as reported.
* **Sequential PK/PD.** The authors fitted the PD model with the
  subject-specific PK predictions fixed. The packaged model joins the two
  so that simulated concentrations drive the parasite model directly,
  which is equivalent for simulation.
* **Rescue treatment and detection limit.** Artemether/lumefantrine
  rescue and the 10 parasites/mL qPCR detection limit are not part of the
  model; simulations continue the parasite dynamics without rescue.
* **Errata.** A search of Europe PMC on 2026-11-24 found no correction or
  erratum for this article.
